a.xlink:title: make_build: reads IDENTITY, DIST_DIR and, when the caller set it, PW_FRESH_BUILD from the make command line or environment; every nonempty SDKROOT, inherited or supplied on the command line, is validated by sdk_guard.sh while parsing the Makefile before any recipe. /usr/bin/make is itself a developer-tool shim and that SDK check runs xcrun, both before build.sh and its native builder check, and both run translated when make does; writes nothing; runs build.sh with them, which a translated make starts translated
a.text: [build] build, sign and embed evidence into …/PolicyWitness.app

a.xlink:title: admission: reads hw.optional.arm64 and sysctl.proc_translated, each read by /usr/sbin/sysctl from the script's own shell before anything else runs (--help included): the build proceeds only on 1 and 0, and an empty value or a failed probe refuses; then BUILD_XPC, PW_INSPECTION, PW_FRESH_BUILD and the argument list (--help prints the usage and exits after the knobs are validated, before any other check); whether each tracked input the build copies exists; the pinned interpreter, /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.14/bin/python3.14, which must be an executable file in a python@3.14 keg that names a 3.14 version and must report that version when probed in isolation, with no PYTHON* variable set other than the three the helpers own, resolved again by the shell front end and by the script under the owner; without a claim in the environment, the caller's SDKROOT, CPATH, LIBRARY_PATH, MANPATH and LC_CTYPE, witnessed by the shell front end's builtins, and tests/.checkout.lock, which the owner it starts directly takes before supervising the script again under it; every nonempty caller SDKROOT must resolve through xcrun to an existing SDK directory with a numeric version before the lock front end or any developer-tool shim starts; writes the owner record in tests/.checkout.lock (pid, start time, acquisition nonce and admission socket identity) for as long as the owner and its protected children hold it; nothing else

lock: reads the channel's socket identity matching the acquisition record and its kernel-reported peer PID matching the acquisition owner and the owner's handoff over the channel the claim names: the held descriptor, open on this checkout's lock file, and the acquisition nonce its owner record carries; never the environment alone; writes nothing
check_limits: reads docs/limits.json and the documents it renders; writes nothing
check_contract: reads docs/contract.json (including the runner protocol and signed service marker), docs/architecture.json and their generated copies; writes nothing
check_build_doc: reads docs/build.json, build.sh, meson.build, the Makefile, the inventories, the baseline and the generated copies; writes nothing
check_identity: reads the identity inputs and the three generated copies; writes nothing

stamp: reads git describe, rev-parse and rev-list, or PW_VERSION and PW_BUILD_NUMBER from the environment; the environment witness compared with the starting environment (SDKROOT supplied from before its removal); writes the four stamp variables for Cargo and the plists; after admitting builddir/, controller/target/, its release/, its aarch64-apple-darwin/ and that directory's release/, and the session destination, controller/target/ when it is missing and the build session file, opened with the stamp, the three knobs, the fixed output target, the acquisition nonce and the build's witnessed starting environment as requests
minimum: reads LSMinimumSystemVersion in Info.plist; writes MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET for Cargo

sdk: reads the SDK path and numeric version xcrun reports under DEVELOPER_DIR for the macosx default, or for the SDK a caller's SDKROOT names; writes SDKROOT for Cargo and Meson, resolved by xcrun, and the SDK version every shipped output must carry

builddir: reads in incremental mode: builddir/meson-info/meson-info.json and builddir/pw-toolchain.json when the directory is configured: its output target (Meson's host machine, the targets' architecture selections and the Cargo triple), compared with the required target and then with Meson's introspection of the directory before any probe, and the stamped SDK, developer directory, compiler commands and Rust compiler probed now; in fresh mode nothing, since the directory is replaced; writes the toolchain observation into the build session
identity: reads IDENTITY and the keychain listing; the knobs, for Meson's options and RUSTFLAGS; writes RUSTFLAGS, when inspection is on and it was unset or empty, and the record of who set it

cargo_admit: reads Cargo's configuration as one invocation from this directory reads it: `.cargo/config` or `config.toml` here, in each ancestor and in Cargo home, with their includes, merged by Cargo's precedence; the environment overrides; the launcher (a rustup proxy and the toolchain it resolves); the output triple the command passes and the lower-precedence target defaults it overrides; and cargo metadata's report of the target and build directories under the pinned target directory; writes the compiler and wrapper selection with its sources, the `[env]` entries and whether each applied, the compiler's inputs in Cargo's child environment, the output triple with the defaults it overrides, the requested Rust flags by precedence, target rules attributed to that triple and the admission, into the build session
a.text: Admitting the Cargo output and intermediate directories: …

a.xlink:title: fresh: reads builddir/, controller/target/release/ and controller/target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/, admitted again with every component below the checkout a real directory of this user, or absent, all before any is removed, and rechecked before each removal; writes removes the three directories through their admitted descriptors; records each one's replacement in the build session; nothing else is removed, including other profiles and other triples

cargo: reads cargo on PATH with its configuration, caches and registries; controller/ sources and the output triple passed with --target, the stamp variables, MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET, SDKROOT and RUSTFLAGS; the artifact paths and per-target reuse judgments Cargo reports, each a literal boolean bound to the shipped target, a typed non-test profile and the admitted executable, and Cargo's fingerprint for each shipped target; each shipped output's container, architecture names and platform, from its header, lipo -archs and its load commands; writes controller/target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/ under the pinned output directory for the shipped executables and controller/target/release/ for build scripts and procedural macros, the messages file Cargo reports its artifacts in, and the output check's observations and the judgments into the build session
toolchain: reads meson and ninja on PATH and ninja's version; writes nothing
a.text: Checking the native toolchain (meson, ninja … or newer)

a.xlink:title: configure: reads whether builddir/build.ninja exists, meson.build, meson.options and the two Meson options; a fresh setup also reads CFLAGS and the other flag variables, and the compilers Meson selected; writes builddir/ configuration; a fresh setup publishes builddir/pw-toolchain.json atomically from the selected compilers, SDK and Rust compiler; meson configure records the two options and the policy assertions run at setup or at the regeneration the next compile triggers
a.text: Configuring native build (meson configure, existing directory): …

a.xlink:title: compile: reads the native sources through builddir/; a changed option triggers regeneration, which runs the policy assertions first; writes builddir/ outputs and the Swift module cache under it

native_check: reads Meson's introspection of builddir/, Ninja's dependency log, the identity inputs, the stamp and the compilers the directory records, and every shipped output's container, architecture names and load commands; writes builddir/pw-toolchain.json extended with the Swift compiler a reused directory discovered when this build enabled the XPC pieces, atomically and without changing another field; the toolchain, option, Meson machine, output target and SDK observations into the build session
a.text: Checking the configured native source lists and the identity closure against the tree

a.xlink:title: assemble: reads Info.plist, the three Rust outputs, runner/augments/, dist/README.md and dist/AGENTS.md, all admitted before the first check; writes the two documents under DIST_DIR; removes the previous app, ZIP and guide; the stamped Info.plist, the three Rust executables and the augments under the new app
embed_client: reads builddir/pw-runner-client; writes Contents/MacOS/pw-runner-client and its dSYM in inspection builds
skip_xpc: reads nothing; writes nothing

embed_services: reads each service's Info.plist and builddir/ host, the worker, validator and issuer; writes each service bundle: its stamped Info.plist, the host with its dSYM in inspection builds, the worker, validator and issuer

assembled: reads the variant's required executable paths even when missing or lacking a Mach-O header, plus every regular file under the assembled app whose header is a Mach-O or fat container, except dSYM companions whose every slice has a complete debug header: its container, lipo -archs names and LC_BUILD_VERSION platform; writes the observations into the build session; nothing in the bundle
a.text: Checking the assembled code against the output target: …

a.xlink:title: presign: reads the identity inputs and copies, the generated identity in tests/lib/contract.py and the built worker's --version report; writes nothing
a.text: Checking host/worker identity again, before signing

a.xlink:title: sign_tools: reads the copied top-level helpers; writes signatures on the top-level helpers
sign_services: reads each service's Entitlements.plist, admitted before the first check, and the assembled bundle; writes signatures on the nested helpers, then each service seal

evidence: reads the signed bytes, entitlements and exported symbols of the helpers, services and augments; the build session; every shipped output's load commands, container, architecture names and signature display; the caller's requests and Cargo's effective deployment target and SDK, from the build session; writes Contents/Resources/Evidence/manifest.json, symbols.json and provenance.json, the manifest listing the other two; the record only after it passes its own validation
a.text: Writing evidence manifest and provenance record

a.xlink:title: seal: reads PolicyWitness.entitlements; writes the app seal over everything under Contents/
verify: reads the sealed app; writes nothing
signer: reads every regular file under the app's and each service's Contents/MacOS, and the app and service seals, as codesign displays them; writes nothing
guide: reads docs/PolicyWitness.md and its inputs; writes PolicyWitness.md under DIST_DIR

zip: reads the sealed app, the variant's required executable paths and any additional code found by header checked against the output target again before the ZIP is written; only debug-only dSYM companions are excluded; writes PolicyWitness.zip under DIST_DIR
